newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia cocoa prices slide on NY plunge.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia cocoa prices slide on NY plunge.

text.p: Indonesian cocoa prices were sharply lower on Wednesday in step with the downtrend in New York futures, prompting sellers to hold back, traders said.
Cocoa was quoted at 2,650-75 rupiah per kg in Ujung Pandang, capital of the key growing region of South Sulawesi, compared with 2,735-50 a week ago and 2,800-50 two weeks ago.
"The market has come down due to falls in New York," one trader said. "The sharp decline has caused farmers to hold back from selling, but they won't stay out for long."
New York cocoa futures slipped to seven-month lows overnight as speculators shed long positions on fundamentals.
Cocoa prices have fallen sharply over the past four sessions in New York as exporters in the key West African producing region ship their first arrivals of the 1996/97 harvest.
Local traders said some players were actively buying to meet outstanding contracts but added that monsoon rains were delaying delivery of the mid-crop harvest.
"Transportation of cocoa from some growing areas has been affected by the rains," one trader said. "But the situation is not serious. We just have to watch out for mouldy beans."
Another trader said cocoa arrivals in South Sulawesi were estimated at 16,800 tonnes in August and 17,330 in September.
He said October arrivals were estimated at between 21,000 and 22,000 tonnes, adding that November arrivals were expected to fall sharply as the mid-crop harvest neared completion.

Meanwhile, a joint project by the Indonesia Cocoa Association (Askindo) and the American Cocoa Research Institute to control the spread of the pod borer pest was officially launched in South Sulawesi on Wednesday.

Askindo figures show the pod borer to have affected 4,568 hectares (11,290 acres) in Central Sulawesi, 300 hectares (740 acres) in the South, 283 hectares (700 acres) in the North, and 65 hectares (160 acres) in Southeast Sulawesi.
